headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors, while Marker’s local-only profile limits direct leakage and write conflicts.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP Server and API surfaces, so its outputs can be bridged into Marker by an orchestrator or manual workflow. Marker is document-processing and may treat file content as input, but neither profile shows a direct shared channel by default. Uncertainty about the bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator forwards MinerU output into Marker as trusted text or files, injection becomes actionable.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared MCP or clipboard bridge, attacker-controlled document text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from MinerU to Marker.
Insert a human review step before Marker consumes MinerU output.
Strip instructions and markup from extracted text before reuse.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is local-only in the profile and has no network egress, while MinerU has allowlisted egress and MCP/API surfaces. The pair does not show shared filesystem access or sensitive data classes, so leakage is possible only through an external workflow, not by default. That keeps blast radius limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace, MinerU can transmit extracted content through its allowlisted egress.
IF the operator routes confidential documents through MinerU APIs, those contents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of MinerU API mode.
Run each agent in a separate directory.
Disable network access for MinerU when processing confidential files.
Review allowlisted destinations before processing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or use MCP; MinerU also cannot write the filesystem or modify git. With no overlapping write surface, there is no plausible conflict over shared mutable state in the default profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is extended to write the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF an external orchestrator grants shared mutable state, the current none verdict no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Do not grant git write access.
Run them in separate sandboxes.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU can emit extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Marker may consume as document input. Marker has no built-in verification surface in the profile, so a bad extraction can cascade into downstream misrendering or incorrect document processing. The interaction is inferred from documented document-processing roles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Marker consumes MinerU output without a verification step, extraction errors can propagate.
IF MinerU OCR or layout output is treated as authoritative, downstream document products may be wrong.
mitigations: Add a validation pass before Marker ingests MinerU output.
Compare extracted text against source PDFs for a sample set.
Flag low-confidence OCR regions for review.
Keep a human approval step for final outputs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are stated in either profile, and both are open-source document-processing tools. MinerU’s allowlisted egress creates a potential compliance concern if regulated data is processed, but Marker’s profile shows no outbound transmission. The mismatch is therefore conditional and limited.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through MinerU’s allowlisted egress, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF the operator requires strict local-only handling, MinerU’s network capability conflicts with that requirement.
mitigations: Process regulated data only in local mode.
Document allowed jurisdictions for MinerU egress.
Avoid sending secrets through either agent.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
